newsitem.title: UK: Branson's Virgin launches internet service.
newsitem.headline: Branson's Virgin launches internet service.

text.p: Virgin chief Richard Branson launched Virgin Net in Britain on Tuesday, billing it as "the first consumer-friendly" internet service provider.

Virgin Net will enable subscribers to use a directory of what Virgin considers to be the internet's 3,000 most useful web pages, or sources of information, as well as providing access to the Internet worldwide computer network.
Virgin Net, the latest addition to Branson's empire which includes an airline, a soft drinks company, financial services and television, is due to go online on November 28.
The monthly subscription will be 10 pounds ($16.75).

Subscribers will be able to access news, sports, games and entertainment channels, one official said. News and informaion organisation Reuters Holdings Plc will be providing news for the service through a third party.
Virgin Communications retains 51 percent of Virgin Net, with CableTel, owning the remaining 49 percent.

Famous for his stunts involving hot air balloons, Branson did not disappoint. Lowered by a crane, he burst through a yellow polystyrene wall painted with the Virgin logo dressed in a silver space suit to launch "Virgin Net."

Asked if Virgin Airline's planes will have access to the internet, Branson said, "We will hopefully have live-television on our planes within the next 12 months." He said he hoped inflight Internet access would follow.
Virgin Net is focussed on Britain, CableTel's managing director, John Gregg, said. It hopes to have about 20,000 subscribers by the end of the year, one official said.

Asked how much Virgin invested in the project, Branson said "You're probably looking at (an investment) of 50 to 100 million sterling between Virgin and CableTel after we've been in the business for four to five years."
"We estimate that Virgin Net will be able to stand alone as a profitable business within a couple of years time," he added.
Virgin Net will use broadband technology, a new technology which allows information such as pictures to be sent along a phone cable far quicker than conventional narrowband lines.

It will also use a customised version of Netscpae Navigator, the internet search engine, which allows users to "surf" the net, and will include "Cybersitter", which will enable parents to screen what their children can access.
